17: package puttyhosts
18: 
19: import (
20: 	"fmt"
21: 	"regexp"
22: 	"strings"
23: 
24: 	"golang.org/x/exp/slices"
25: )
26: 
27: func hostnameContainsDot(hostname string) bool {
28: 	return strings.Contains(hostname, ".")
29: }
30: 
31: func hostnameisWildcard(hostname string) bool {
32: 	return strings.HasPrefix(hostname, "*.")
33: }
34: 
35: func wildcardFromHostname(hostname string) string {
36: 	if hostnameisWildcard(hostname) {
37: 		return hostname
38: 	}
39: 	// prevent a panic below if the string doesn't contain a hostname. this should never happen,
40: 	// as this function is only intended to be called after checking hostnameContainsDot.
41: 	if !hostnameContainsDot(hostname) {
42: 		return hostname
43: 	}
44: 	return fmt.Sprintf("*.%s", strings.Join(strings.Split(hostname, ".")[1:], "."))
45: }
46: 
47: // AddHostToHostList adds a new hostname to PuTTY's list of trusted hostnames for a given host CA.
48: //
49: // Background:
50: //   - For every host CA that it is configured to trust, PuTTY maintains a list of hostnames (hostList) which it should consider
51: //     to be valid for that host CA. This is the same as the @cert-authority lines in an `~/.ssh/known_hosts` file.
52: //   - Trusted hostnames can be individual entries (host1, host2) or wildcards like "*.example.com".
53: //   - PuTTY keeps this list of hostnames stored against each host CA in the Windows registry. It exposes a GUI (under
54: //     Connection -> SSH -> Host Keys -> Configure Host CAs at the time of writing) which expects any new host CAs and
55: //     trusted hostnames for each to be added manually by end users as part of session configuration.
56: //   - This process is mandatory for validation of host CAs in PuTTY to work, but is a cumbersome manual process with many
57: //     clicks required in a nested interface. Instead, this function is called as part of `tsh puttyconfig` to examine the
58: //     existing list of trusted hostnames and automate the process of adding a new valid hostname to a given host CA.
59: //
60: // Connection flow:
61: //   - When connecting to a host which presents a host CA, PuTTY searches its list of CAs to find any which are considered
62: //     valid for that hostname, then checks whether the host's presented CA matches any of them. If there is a CA -> hostname
63: //     match, the connection will continue successfully. If not, an error will be shown.
64: //
65: // Intended operation of this function:
66: //   - This function is passed the current list of trusted hostnames for a given host CA (retrieved from the registry), along
67: //     with a new hostname entry (from tsh puttyconfig <hostname>) which should be added to the list.
68: //   - It appends the new hostname to the end of the hostList
69: //   - All hostnames in the hostList are converted to their wildcard form if they contain a dot (test.example.com -> *.example.com)
70: //     and are grouped together.
71: //   - If a wildcard group only contains a single hostname which would be matched by its wildcard equivalent, that hostname is added
72: //     to the hostList verbatim to prevent inadvertently matching against too many hosts with the same wildcard.
73: //   - If a wildcard matches more than one hostname, the wildcard will be added to the hostList instead and the single hostnames
74: //     discarded.
75: //   - The hostList is then sorted alphabetically and returned.
76: //
77: // This is an effort to keep the length of hostList as short as possible for efficiency and tidiness, while not using any more
78: // wildcards than necessary and preventing the need for end users to manually configure their trusted host CAs.
79: func AddHostToHostList(hostList []string, hostname string) []string {
80: 	// add the incoming hostname to the hostList before we sort and process it
81: 	hostList = append(hostList, hostname)
82: 
83: 	hostMap := make(map[string][]string)
84: 	// iterate over the full hostList
85: 	// if the element is a wildcard, add it to the list of wildcards
86: 	// if the element is not a wildcard, convert it to a wildcard and add any hostnames it matches to a map
87: 	for _, element := range hostList {
88: 		// FQDN-based hosts are grouped under a wildcard key
89: 		if hostnameContainsDot(element) {
90: 			wildcard := wildcardFromHostname(element)
91: 			if !slices.Contains(hostMap[wildcard], element) {
92: 				hostMap[wildcard] = append(hostMap[wildcard], element)
93: 			}
94: 		} else {
95: 			// any non-wildcard hosts go into the "extra" key and will be processed separately at the end
96: 			hostMap["extra"] = append(hostMap["extra"], element)
97: 		}
98: 	}
99: 
100: 	// iterate over the map, look for all wildcard keys with more than one hostname matching.
101: 	// for each match, add the wildcard to the hostList.
102: 	var outputHostList []string
103: 	for key, matchingHostnames := range hostMap {
104: 		// add all non-wildcard matches separately
105: 		if key == "extra" {
106: 			for _, hostname := range matchingHostnames {
107: 				if !slices.Contains(outputHostList, hostname) {
108: 					outputHostList = append(outputHostList, hostname)
109: 				}
110: 			}
111: 		} else {
112: 			// add all wildcards with more than one hostname matching
113: 			if len(matchingHostnames) > 1 {
114: 				outputHostList = append(outputHostList, key)
115: 			} else {
116: 				// add the single hostname which is matched by the given wildcard
117: 				outputHostList = append(outputHostList, matchingHostnames[0])
118: 			}
119: 		}
120: 	}
121: 
122: 	slices.Sort(outputHostList)
123: 	return outputHostList
124: }
125: 
126: var hostnameRegexp = regexp.MustCompile("^(([a-zA-Z0-9]|[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9]).)*([A-Za-z0-9]|[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])$")
127: 
128: // NaivelyValidateHostname checks the provided hostname against a naive regex to ensure it doesn't contain obviously
129: // illegal characters. It's not guaranteed to be perfect, just a simple sanity check.
130: func NaivelyValidateHostname(hostname string) bool {
131: 	return hostnameRegexp.Match([]byte(hostname))
132: }
